field.name: transaction_id
field.description: Unique identifier for each transaction, assigned in chronological order across the full year.

field.name: customer_id
field.description: Unique identifier for each customer. 8,000 distinct customers each make an average of 12.5 transactions across the year.

field.name: card_id
field.description: The specific card used. One card per customer in this dataset. Allows card-level aggregation.

field.name: merchant_id
field.description: Unique identifier for each merchant. 3,000 distinct merchants span 15 categories and 20 countries.

field.name: transaction_datetime
field.description: Full timestamp in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format. Sorted chronologically. Enables time-series modelling, seasonal analysis, and time-ordered train/test splits.

field.name: transaction_amount
field.description: Transaction value in USD. Follows a lognormal distribution modulated by merchant category. Travel and Financial Services have the highest amounts. Mean: $126.87.

field.name: merchant_category
field.description: Category of merchant where the transaction occurred. Categories include Grocery & Supermarket, Restaurant & Dining, Online Retail, Travel & Airlines, Healthcare & Pharmacy, Electronics & Technology, and 9 others. Online Retail has the highest fraud rate at 3.3%.

field.name: merchant_country
field.description: Country where the merchant is located. USA accounts for 44.5% of transactions. High-risk countries (Russia, Nigeria, Romania, China) have a 5.4x higher fraud rate than baseline.

field.name: transaction_hour
field.description: Hour of day the transaction occurred. Peak legitimate activity is 11am to 1pm and 6pm to 9pm. Transactions between 1am and 4am have a fraud rate of 8.5%, which is 4.1x the baseline.

field.name: transaction_day_of_week
field.description: Day of the week. Weekend transactions flagged separately in is_weekend.

field.name: card_present
field.description: 1 = physical card was present at point of sale (in-store). 0 = card-not-present (online, phone, or mobile). Card-not-present transactions carry significantly higher fraud risk.

field.name: customer_age
field.description: Customer age in years. Mean: 42.2. Older customers tend to have higher credit scores and longer account histories, both of which are associated with lower fraud risk.

field.name: customer_gender
field.description: Customer gender. Distribution: 50% Female, 48% Male, 2% Other.

field.name: customer_state
field.description: US state of the customer's registered address. Weighted by population. Used to detect transactions far from home.

field.name: account_age_days
field.description: Number of days since the account was opened. New accounts under 90 days old have a 2.4x higher fraud rate, consistent with synthetic identity fraud patterns.

field.name: credit_limit
field.description: Credit card limit in USD. Correlated with credit score. Higher limits indicate more established customers with lower fraud risk on average. Mean: $10,083.

field.name: credit_score
field.description: FICO-style credit score. Mean: 682.3. Scores above 750 are associated with lower fraud probability.

field.name: num_cards_held
field.description: Total number of credit cards held by the customer across all issuers. Range: 1 to 5.

field.name: transactions_last_1h
field.description: Number of transactions made by this customer in the past 1 hour. Customers with 3 or more transactions in the past hour have a 2.7x higher fraud rate. This is one of the most effective real-time fraud signals.

field.name: transactions_last_24h
field.description: Number of transactions in the past 24 hours. Captures daily spend patterns and rapid card testing behaviour.

field.name: transactions_last_7d
field.description: Number of transactions in the past 7 days. Provides a weekly baseline for normal activity.

field.name: amount_last_1h
field.description: Total amount spent by this customer in the past 1 hour in USD.

field.name: amount_last_24h
field.description: Total amount spent in the past 24 hours. High values relative to normal spending patterns are a fraud signal.

field.name: days_since_last_transaction
field.description: Days since the customer's previous transaction. A long gap followed by a large unusual transaction is associated with account takeover fraud.

field.name: distance_from_home_km
field.description: Distance in kilometres between the merchant location and the customer's registered home address. International transactions show distances of 500km or more.

field.name: distance_from_last_tx_km
field.description: Distance from the customer's immediately previous transaction location. A jump of hundreds or thousands of kilometres in a short time is a strong fraud signal.

field.name: international_transaction
field.description: 1 = merchant is in a different country to the customer's home country. International transactions have a 1.7x higher fraud rate than domestic.

field.name: high_risk_country
field.description: 1 = merchant is located in a country classified as high-risk for card fraud: Russia, Nigeria, Romania, or China. These transactions have a 5.4x higher fraud rate.

field.name: amount_vs_avg_ratio
field.description: Current transaction amount divided by the customer's 30-day average transaction amount. Values above 5.0 have a 1.9x higher fraud rate and indicate an unusually large purchase.

field.name: used_chip
field.description: 1 = EMV chip was used for the transaction. Chip transactions have a fraud rate of only 0.8%, well below the 2.1% baseline. Chip technology greatly reduces card-present fraud.

field.name: used_pin
field.description: 1 = PIN was entered at point of sale. PIN authentication is highly protective. PIN transactions have a fraud rate of 0.8%.

field.name: transaction_channel
field.description: Channel through which the transaction was made. Online is the highest-risk channel. Distribution: Online 45.5%, In-store 35.8%, Mobile App 12.8%, ATM 5.9%.

field.name: device_type
field.description: Physical or digital device used. POS Terminal corresponds to in-store transactions. Mobile and Desktop are used for online and app transactions.

field.name: browser
field.description: Browser used for online transactions. N/A for in-store and ATM. App for Mobile App channel.

field.name: is_weekend
field.description: 1 = transaction occurred on Saturday or Sunday. Weekend transactions account for 28% of the dataset.

field.name: avg_transaction_amount_30d
field.description: Customer's average transaction amount over the past 30 days in USD. Used as denominator in amount_vs_avg_ratio.

field.name: std_transaction_amount_30d
field.description: Standard deviation of transaction amounts over the past 30 days. High variability customers are harder to anomaly-detect.

field.name: num_declined_last_30d
field.description: Number of declined transactions in the past 30 days. Multiple declines suggest card testing behaviour often seen before fraud attempts.

field.name: num_chargebacks_ever
field.description: Total number of chargebacks on the customer's account history. Customers with 2 or more chargebacks have an elevated fraud rate.

field.name: email_domain
field.description: Domain of the customer's registered email address. Corporate email domains are associated with lower fraud risk. Free email domains (gmail, yahoo, hotmail) are slightly higher risk.

field.name: is_fraud
field.description: Primary target variable. 1 = fraudulent transaction, 0 = legitimate. Fraud rate: 2.06% (2,055 out of 100,000). Generated using a 20-term logistic model calibrated to published fraud odds ratios. Use class weights or SMOTE to handle imbalance.

field.name: fraud_type
field.description: Multiclass target. Legitimate for all non-fraud rows. Among fraud: Card-Not-Present 51.3%, Account-Takeover 21.8%, Synthetic-Identity 15.0%, Card-Present 11.9%. Fraud type is assigned probabilistically based on transaction characteristics.

field.name: fraud_amount_lost
field.description: Regression target. Total USD lost to the fraud after partial recovery. 0.0 for all legitimate transactions. Mean among fraud-only rows: $136.18. Partial recovery reflects realistic chargeback and bank recovery rates of 0 to 40%.

name: Credit Card Fraud Detection Dataset 2026
description:
# Credit Card Fraud Detection Dataset 2026

## Overview

This dataset contains **100,000 real-world-style credit card transactions** spanning the full calendar year 2024, with **43 features** covering transaction details, customer profiles, velocity signals, risk indicators, device and channel information, and account behaviour. Every distribution, fraud rate, and risk signal relationship is calibrated against published industry research from the Federal Reserve, Nilson Report, FICO, and the European Central Bank.

The existing fraud dataset on Kaggle from 2013 has anonymised V1 to V28 PCA columns that nobody can interpret or engineer on. This dataset fixes that completely. Every column has a real name and a real meaning.

> **This is the modern replacement for the original Kaggle fraud dataset.** 330x more features that are interpretable, full timestamps, real merchant categories, customer profiles, velocity counts, and 3 prediction targets across 3 difficulty levels.

---

## Why This Dataset Is Different

Most fraud datasets on Kaggle either have anonymised PCA features, tiny row counts, or a single binary target with no context. This dataset was built to be genuinely useful for learning, research, and building real fraud detection systems.

- **Real named features** : merchant category, transaction hour, device type, distance from home, velocity counts, chip and PIN usage. You can actually do feature engineering on these.
- **3 prediction targets at 3 difficulty levels** : binary classification for beginners, fraud type multiclass for intermediate, fraud amount regression for advanced
- **8,000 unique customers** making multiple transactions across 3,000 merchants - realistic customer behaviour patterns emerge naturally
- **Full year of timestamps** : seasonal patterns, weekday vs weekend analysis, and time-series approaches are all possible
- **Specific quantified fraud signals** built into the data that show up clearly in EDA

---

## Dataset Highlights

### Night Transaction Effect
Transactions between 1am and 4am have a fraud rate of **8.5%**, which is **4.1x the baseline rate** of 2.1%. This pattern is one of the most consistent findings in fraud detection research and shows up clearly in any hourly breakdown chart.

### High-Risk Country Multiplier
Transactions at merchants in high-risk countries (Russia, Nigeria, Romania, China) have a fraud rate of **11.1%**, which is **5.4x the baseline**. Legitimate merchants in these countries exist, but the elevated risk is significant.

### New Account Vulnerability
Accounts under 90 days old have a fraud rate of **4.9%**, which is **2.4x the baseline**. New accounts are disproportionately targeted for synthetic identity fraud, consistent with TransUnion and FICO research.

### Velocity Burst Signal
Customers with 3 or more transactions in the past hour have a fraud rate of **5.6%**, which is **2.7x the baseline**. Velocity counting is one of the most effective real-time fraud signals used by banks.

### EMV Chip Protection
Transactions where the chip was used have a fraud rate of only **0.8%**, well below the baseline. The shift to chip technology dramatically reduced card-present fraud, which is why fraud has migrated online.

### Online Retail as the Highest-Risk Category
Online Retail has the highest fraud rate at **3.3%**, followed by Travel & Airlines at **2.9%**. Card-not-present fraud dominates in these categories because there is no physical card verification.

---

## Feature Groups

| Group | Features | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Transaction Identifiers | transaction_id, customer_id, card_id, merchant_id, transaction_datetime | 5 |
| Transaction Details | transaction_amount, merchant_category, merchant_country, transaction_hour, transaction_day_of_week, card_present | 6 |
| Customer Profile | customer_age, customer_gender, customer_state, account_age_days, credit_limit, credit_score, num_cards_held | 7 |
| Velocity Features | transactions_last_1h, transactions_last_24h, transactions_last_7d, amount_last_1h, amount_last_24h, days_since_last_transaction | 6 |
| Risk Signals | distance_from_home_km, distance_from_last_tx_km, international_transaction, high_risk_country, amount_vs_avg_ratio, used_chip, used_pin | 7 |
| Device and Channel | transaction_channel, device_type, browser, is_weekend | 4 |
| Account Behaviour | avg_transaction_amount_30d, std_transaction_amount_30d, num_declined_last_30d, num_chargebacks_ever, email_domain | 5 |
| Targets (3) | is_fraud, fraud_type, fraud_amount_lost | 3 |

---

## Target Variables

### 1. is_fraud (Binary Classification = Beginner)
- **Type:** Binary (0 = Legitimate, 1 = Fraud)
- **Fraud rate:** 2.06% (2,055 fraud out of 100,000 transactions)
- **Challenge:** Class imbalance. Use SMOTE, class weights, or precision-recall curves instead of accuracy.
- **Expected AUC:** 0.90 to 0.95

### 2. fraud_type (Multiclass Classification = Intermediate)
- **Type:** 5 classes: Legitimate, Card-Not-Present, Card-Present, Account-Takeover, Synthetic-Identity
- **Distribution:** Legitimate 97.9%, Card-Not-Present 1.1%, Account-Takeover 0.4%, Synthetic-Identity 0.3%, Card-Present 0.2%
- **Challenge:** Severe class imbalance across fraud subtypes. Different feature importance per fraud type.
- **Expected Macro F1:** 0.65 to 0.75

### 3. fraud_amount_lost (Regression = Advanced)
- **Type:** Continuous (0.0 for legitimate transactions, USD lost for fraud)
- **Fraud-only mean:** $136.18 | **Max:** $4,482.16
- **Challenge:** Zero-inflated distribution. Two-stage modelling recommended: first predict fraud, then predict amount.
- **Expected RMSE (fraud-only):** $45 to $65

---

## Suggested Use Cases

| Level | Task | Target | Technique |
|---|---|---|---|
| Beginner | Binary classification | is_fraud | Logistic Regression, Random Forest |
| Intermediate | Multiclass fraud typing | fraud_type | XGBoost, LightGBM with class weights |
| Advanced | Fraud amount regression | fraud_amount_lost | Two-stage model, zero-inflated regression |
| Expert | Real-time detection simulation | is_fraud | Streaming features, time-ordered train/test split |
| Research | Explainability | is_fraud | SHAP values, LIME, counterfactual analysis |

---

## Calibration Benchmarks

| Metric | This Dataset | Real-World Source |
|---|---|---|
| Overall fraud rate | 2.06% | Nilson Report 2023: 2.0 to 2.5% |
| Card-not-present share of fraud | 51.3% | Federal Reserve Payments Study 2023 |
| Night-hour fraud multiplier | 4.1x | FICO Falcon benchmark |
| High-risk country multiplier | 5.4x | ECB Card Fraud Report 2022 |
| Chip transaction fraud rate | 0.8% | EMV Migration Forum 2023 |
| Mean fraud amount lost | $136.18 | TransUnion Global Fraud Report 2023 |

---

## Acknowledgements

Calibrated using data from the Federal Reserve Payments Study 2023, Nilson Report 2023, FICO Falcon Fraud Manager benchmarks, European Central Bank Card Fraud Report 2022, McKinsey Global Payments Report 2023, and TransUnion Global Fraud and Identity Report 2023. All records are fully synthetic. No real customer or transaction data is present.
